workshops.title: Firebase notebook: policy, rules, and integration workshop
workshops.summary: Run an offline account-owned notebook policy, add one independent failure case, and follow separate Firebase SDK and rules-emulator integration gates.

sections.title: Start with the offline contract and predict its states
sections.html:
A contract states the inputs a component accepts and the outcomes it promises. This companion begins with ordinary Swift contracts for a synthetic notebook. Alice owns n1 with title Lantern and revision 0. Bob must not receive Alice's rows. A stale edit cannot replace a newer title. Media and messaging helpers return bounded decisions and effects rather than contacting any service.

Open the README, Host/Policy.swift and Host/Checks.swift. The two Host files compile directly with Swift 6 and Foundation on the development computer. No Swift package graph or remote dependency exists in that compile. Use the README's scratch output path and module cache. Run the executable and retain the compiler version and actual result.

The supplied authoring baseline passes 55 checks. Before copying that result, predict the current snapshot, Alice-to-Bob switch, same-UID relogin, stale revision, overlap and token-detachment cases. Baseline execution is reference evidence; the learner must make an independent change and verify it. No practice submission or progress state is marked complete.

sections.title: Add an independent stale-error schedule
sections.html:
A stale result belongs to work that no longer owns the visible state. SessionStamp carries a UID and generation. switchAccount advances the generation and clears rows. accept first compares the captured stamp, then validates owner and stable IDs, then replaces the complete snapshot. A mixed foreign snapshot cannot partially enter the display.

Implement an error-publication method in a scratch copy. Capture Alice generation 1, switch to Bob generation 2, accept Bob's current note, then deliver Alice's old failure. Bob's rows and status must remain unchanged. Return Alice at generation 3 and reject the original reply again. Use controlled method calls, not timing sleeps.

Add a separate page request generation for one-shot history. Request A begins, request B begins, B succeeds, A fails. The latest request's success must survive. PagePolicy.merge checks overlap and revisions but does not own request identity or Firestore sorting. Preserve that distinction while deciding frozen-history versus refresh semantics.

The Kotlin comparison is a StateFlow with request identity checked before an update. Coroutine cancellation and Swift Task cancellation can reduce work but cannot make an already queued callback disappear. Listener/task removal and publication guards both need named owners. The independent schedule tests a real failure policy instead of merely asserting a helper returns its own constant.

The current host also supplies PublicationPolicy and CreatePolicy checks. Implement your own visible status/error adapter and request schedules rather than copying their results. Native create retains a pending ID, reads its owned document from the server before retry, and stops publication when account or request lifetime changes.

sections.title: Read real rules and prepare interpreter fixtures
sections.html:
Rules/firestore.rules and Rules/storage.rules are actual Firebase Security Rules sources. They are separate from the Swift authorization model. Firestore permits account-owned notes with exact fields, types, revision transitions and server timestamps, and bounded list queries. Storage permits private immutable JPEG-declared objects with owner metadata and byte limits, while denying updates and listing.

The Node fixture uses initializeTestEnvironment, authenticatedContext and unauthenticatedContext to send real local service requests. It asserts owner CRUD, direct anonymous and Bob denial, malformed documents, stale revisions, list limits and unknown-path denial. Storage checks MIME, owner metadata, zero/maximum/excess bytes, overwrite, metadata transfer and delete rights.

Mocked token identities are appropriate for an authorization suite. They do not establish actual Apple/Google/provider sign-in, but a provisioned fixture run executes the rules interpreter. A Swift host authorize check does not. The fixture clears both services between cases and tears down the environment so leftover objects do not change later operation semantics.

Do not install Node modules or start/download missing emulator binaries in this assignment. The README's gated command is for an already provisioned local environment using demo-firebase-course and loopback ports. This author checked Node syntax only. Add one direct whitespace-title or ID fixture as learner work, and record actual interpreter results only when that gate runs.

sections.title: Integrate the actual SwiftUI notebook separately
sections.html:
The SDK directory supplies a real SwiftUI App entry, emulator bootstrap, Firestore repository and Storage adapter. Create a scratch iOS target, include the exact listed files, attach the provisioned Core/Auth/Firestore/Storage products, and set FIREBASE_SDK_LAB. Exclude Host/Checks.swift and the generated duplicate app entry. The README records the target's language/isolation/deployment choices.

The Connect local services button configures a named demo app. It does not prove a successful request. A separate button creates an example.invalid account in the Auth emulator, then Add note uses a Firestore transaction and a bounded live listener. The source is not a prebuilt or executed native app. The SDK modules were not resolved or typechecked during authoring.

Independently add revision-edit and delete controls that preserve stable IDs, retain drafts on conflict and recheck account ownership on async completion. The repository supplies those service methods, but no claim is made that their complete interaction ran. Test a stopped emulator and denied request as well as the happy path.

The media adapter starts after image preparation and uses bounded Data. It is not a full picker or image editor. Cancellation requires caller account/request checks. The current Firestore rules deny media manifests, so do not declare upload plus publication complete without designing and executing that additional schema/rule integration.

The screen serializes authentication submissions and guards both success and error after await. Pending create state is in memory, not restart-safe storage. Ordinary Remote Config failure returns active/default selection plus a diagnostic; cancellation remains explicit. Remote Storage needs Blaze and its actual configured bucket, and Firebase App Attest requires the production entitlement.

sections.title: Review optional services and partial-success ownership
sections.html:
ProductionServices.swift is a different gate, FIREBASE_PRODUCTION_SERVICES, and belongs to a separately reviewed target. It covers APNs token forwarding, collection setters, custom traces, Remote Config defaults, App Check factory setup, callable requests and connection-aware Realtime Database presence. Those services do not all route through the notebook's three emulators.

Functions/cleanup.mjs supplies actual callable and worker sources. It derives ownership from authenticated context, stores a stable command under a user namespace, rejects payload-changing command reuse, and deletes the derived owner path only with the original generation precondition before recording an outcome. A replay reconciles absence or preserves a replacement after deletion and recreation. It requires separately provisioned Functions/Admin dependencies and explicit runtime configuration; no invocation or deployment ran.

Rules/database.rules.json supplies a private presence policy with separately gated, unexecuted presence.test.mjs interpreter fixtures. PresenceOwner checks a generation before advertising online after disconnect registration. Its owner must stop it before credential replacement and verify cleanup acknowledgement, reconnect and old-registration behavior. An online signal describes connection, not human attention.

Write a recovery matrix for ambiguous create, stale edit, listener failure, uploadedUnpublished media, lost token-detachment acknowledgement and account deletion. The host models are in memory. They do not prove restart-safe persistence, backend job retries, symbol uploads, provider credentials, quotas or costs.

Cleanup stores the original generation string and uses a conditional delete. Run the pure cleanup-policy.test.mjs fixture independently: its eight synthetic schedules cover large adjacent generations, lost progress acknowledgement, recreated paths and provider-error propagation. It imports no Firebase SDK. Also predict discardLocalDraft and removeDanglingManifest before executing the host boundaries.

sections.title: Build an evidence ledger another person can trust
sections.html:
Record each gate as passed, failed or pending with its exact command, toolchain and scope. Authoring evidence is 55 offline policy checks, Swift syntax parsing for the gated adapters and Node syntax checks for fixture/server sources. The unit and bank JSON receive bounded schema/content checks. Main owns shared registration, rendering and full-course validation.

Use official release notes for SDK compatibility, and inspect the exact selected provider/Functions runtime releases later. Do not claim that a compiler version proves an arbitrary dependency graph works. A composite-index emulator query pass also does not establish a deployed index or production transaction limit.

State the independent change's before/after prediction and observed result. Keep all data synthetic and all learner completion pending. The handoff includes the source list, target settings, current rules limitations, gate commands and the pending SDK, emulator, simulator, provider and optional-service matrix. No download, authentication, remote account setup or deployment is necessary to make that report reviewable.

Keep 55 host policy checks and eight pure cleanup tests as separate executed rows. Node syntax passes for Functions and emulator sources remain parsing evidence. A mocked object store's generation check does not establish real conditional deletion, just as a mock UID check does not establish rules execution.

exercise.brief: Extend the offline notebook with stale-error rejection, then prepare a concrete integration handoff for the real SDK and rules.
steps: Run and record the supplied host baseline.
Implement a current/stale error state and the Alice/Bob/Alice schedule in a scratch copy.
Add one direct malformed rules fixture with an allowed counterpart; leave execution pending if runtime is unavailable.
Plan revision-edit controls and media-manifest schema as separately gated native work.
Produce the evidence/recovery table, with sourced version decisions and named next checks.
Run the pure generation replay fixture and independently add a concurrent replacement schedule without initializing Firebase.
acceptance: The new old-error case preserves Bob's newer rows and status.
The same-UID relogin still rejects the first lifetime's reply.
Direct forbidden requests are specified for actual rules evaluation.
Native/service claims are bounded by actual executed evidence.
No learner state, client source, dependency download, login or deployment is changed.
The handoff distinguishes exact generation strings and synthetic replay outcomes from actual provider execution.
exercise.solution:
Use a status field owned by SessionModel and an acceptError method that checks the captured stamp before mutation. At generation 2, accepting Bob's success sets his rows and current status. Deliver Alice generation 1's failure; the method returns false and changes nothing. Generation 3 for Alice's return also rejects generation 1. The test controls call order explicitly.

Add a rules-hardening pair such as an agreed valid ASCII note ID and a forbidden ID under Alice's own path. State that current rules do not restrict noteID, so the new rule and fixtures must change together. Host path validation is not substitute evidence. Preserve owner CRUD and cross-account denial checks during that change.

The native plan includes one @main App, exact source membership, Core/Auth/Firestore/Storage products and FIREBASE_SDK_LAB. Revision editing captures expected revision and preserves the draft on conflict. Media publication requires a manifest policy absent from current note rules. Optional remote services and Functions/RTDB use their own provisioned gates.

Your ledger records the supplied baseline separately from your new checks. Rules interpreter, SDK typecheck/build, simulator, image rendering, provider exchange, APNs, consent persistence, symbolication, traces, App Check, Functions and RTDB are pending unless you independently execute them in an authorized environment. A copied answer does not constitute learner completion.

Use p1/g1 for the retained cleanup intent, then recreate the same path with g2 before replay. The synthetic precondition returns replacementPreserved and keeps g2. An actual Storage integration must independently verify the API option, exact generation transport and provider errors. Add a new schedule yourself; the supplied eight tests are baseline evidence.

quiz.question: What does the workshop's Host implementation label mean?
options: Its runnable baseline executes local Swift contracts; SDK/rules are separate gates
It is a complete native photo app
quiz.explanation: The baseline is executable without Firebase. Real adapter and rules sources remain available but require their own runtimes and evidence.

quiz.question: What is a useful independent modification?
options: An old error after a new success with asserted unchanged current state
Renaming a constant without changing behavior
Copying the worked answer and marking complete
quiz.explanation: A controlled failure schedule verifies a substantive publication contract that the existing baseline does not already prove.

quiz.question: When can the evidence ledger say Firebase rules passed?
options: After the provisioned rules fixture actually executes and assertions pass
quiz.explanation: Parsing does not execute imports or interpreter assertions. Record the actual service/test command and results.

simple.story: A workshop builds a model cupboard and tests who may place drawings on each shelf. It also prepares instructions and keys for a real cupboard, but keeps those tools in a separate box. A learner changes the model so a late message from yesterday cannot change today's tray. The learner records that observed result and lists the real cupboard tests still waiting for equipment. The report helps the next person continue without assuming every tool was already used.
simple.meaning: The workshop has a runnable offline baseline plus separately gated real Firebase sources. The learner independently changes a failure policy and records exact evidence limits.

example.before: Bob's current success is visible at generation 2; Alice's old error carries generation 1.
example.change: Deliver the old error through the new error-publication method.
example.after: The stamp comparison rejects it, leaving Bob's rows and status unchanged.

words.meaning: An explicit set of inputs, outcomes and responsibilities.
Allowing a result to change the current visible state.
A separate target/runtime boundary needed for a particular kind of check.
A retry of the same intent that does not duplicate its external effect.

simple.remember: Run the model honestly, change it independently, and give real integrations their own evidence.
simple.boundary: The cupboard model does not execute SDK calls or Firebase rules. The supplied baseline and worked solution do not record learner completion or prove persisted/service behavior.
